en: Preface to the Catalogue of the Avataṃsaka School’s Commentaries and Treatises, as well as the Records on Hetuvidyā (Logic), Compiled by the Great Dharma Master Enchō of Tōdai-ji in Accordance with the Imperial Edict of the Sovereign.
I humbly consider that the rise of the Buddha-dharma has its origins here [in this land]. In the realm of the Western Heavens, Śākya...
Kāśyapa Muni opened the Deer Park to trace its source;
during the Eastern Han dynasty,
Emperor Xiaoming dreamed of a golden man and followed his traces.
Wondrous images have arrived at our borders,
and the teachings of the subtle word are heard from afar.
In the thirteenth year of the reign of Emperor Kinmei, who resided at the Kishigami-Kinkura Palace, the Buddha-dharma first began to be transmitted.
Thereafter, until the fourteenth year of the Enki era—
three hundred and fifty-three years having passed—
the traditions transmitted during that interval were as follows.
The entirety of the Dharma-treasury has been preserved,
and its teachings have been categorized into their various branches;
the copying of sutras and treatises is vied for both in public and private circles.
Regarding the esoteric and exoteric commentaries and treatises, they were left merely to the whims of human hearts;
sometimes they were kept secret and not transmitted,
and sometimes they were scattered and not transcribed.
The commentaries and treatises of various schools have gradually become so numerous that they obstruct and block the path;

thus, the teachings of the White Horse Temple have no means by which to be explained. We humbly beseech Your Majesty, the Emperor of Meditative Concentration, who before the presence of five hundred Buddhas...
He personally received the entrustment [of the Dharma].
Throughout the world, he manifested as a sovereign deity (*sokujin*),
and his veneration of the holy teachings far surpassed that of the Five Indies.
The flourishing of both the Exoteric and Esoteric teachings has recently doubled that of China.
Consequently, by imperial decree, the various petitions and memorials were transcribed,
and eminent scholars from the six schools were commissioned to present the records of their respective traditions.
Yuanchao, being but a humble student at the periphery of the Huayan tradition,
has humbly presented these records on our own school’s tenets and the science of logic (*hetuvidyā*).
I now prostrate myself, entrusting them to the rectification of future scholars.
Respectfully preface this on the eighth day of the fourth month in the year of Jiashu (494 CE).

The *Daśabhūmivibhāṣā-śāstra* in sixteen fascicles was composed by the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna and translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yaśas of the Later Qin together with Kumārajīva. This work explains the "Ten Stages" (*Daśabhūmi*) up to the Second Stage;

it constitutes one portion of the *Mahā-acintya-sūtra*. The *Daśabhūmi-vibhāṣā-śāstra* in ten fascicles was composed by the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna and translated by Kumārajīva. The *Daśabhūmi-śāstra* in ten fascicles [was composed by Vasubandhu and] translated by Bodhiruci.
*Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, twenty fascicles, composed by Vasubandhu Bodhisattva and translated by Bodhiruci; *Avataṃsaka-sūtra-śāstra*, six hundred fascicles;

The *Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks* states that Dharma Master Huiyuan of Mount Lu established five categories of dharma—namely, teaching, meaning, defilement, purity, and miscellaneous causes—based on the *Sanlun*, *Huayan*, and the "Ten Stages" chapter.

These are now included in this record. *Treatise on the Provisional and Real Meaning of Mahāyāna* (*Dacheng quan shi yi*), two fascicles; composed by Huiyuan. *Mahāyāna Śamatha-vipaśyanā*, one fascicle; composed by Tanqian. *Śamatha-vipaśyanā*, two fascicles; composed by the Zen Master Zhiyi, also known as Zhiyi.

composed by Yuanxiao. *A Collection for Guarding Against Forgetfulness*, ten fascicles; composed by Wenchao. *A Record of the Outline*, two fascicles. *A Treatise on the Harmonization of Disputes through the Ten Gates*, one fascicle;

The above are the extant works.
Thus far, there are one hundred and eighty-two works comprising seven hundred and eighty-four fascicles.
